text:
jia: FYI escalation from Acme — long streaming response gets everything but the final chunk after their token swap, payload is truncated and there's no finish_reason in the last event. customer hit this in prod twice in the last hour. attaching logs and repro steps below. :eyes:

marco: can you paste the curl/websocket output they saw? also which infra (cloudfront/fastly/azure)?

jia: they use our hosted API via a CloudFront fronting proxy. here's their minimal curl reproducer and the tail of the http/1.1 response they captured:

```
# repro (curl)
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-x" \
  --max-time 300
```

```
> GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-x HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< content-type: text/event-stream
<
data: {"delta": "..."}\n\n
# last bytes they received (literal capture)
data: {"delta": "final tokens"}\n\n
# then connection close, no finishing event like {"finish_reason":...} and no final JSON object terminated (client parse error)
```

sophia: quick thought — CloudFront has an idle timeout that can terminate long-lived connections when the origin is idle for N seconds during a token rotation. If token swap causes a tiny pause while auth is refreshed, that can spill into a lost final chunk. Also check buffer/stream flush at the origin. :facepalm:

marco: agree. also need to rule out client abort behavior on 401 -> refresh -> retry that reuses the same TCP connection incorrectly. Connor, you mentioned a node-fetch client earlier? any chance your client closes streams prematurely during a token refresh?

connor: here's the snippet from our mobile client code — we do a fetch with streaming and on 401 we attempt auth refresh, then re-attach event handlers. simplified: 

```
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
if (res.status === 401) {
  await auth.refresh();
  // naive: try to reconnect on same stream
  return fetch(url, opts);
}
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {value, done} = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // append chunk
}
```

connor: we noticed that when refresh runs, the underlying connection can get reset and the browser sometimes emits done without full flush. not sure how that interacts with finish_reason.

marco: that client pattern can cause a half-closed TCP state where the proxy thinks response is complete. two parallel tracks: (1) server-side ensure final event is explicitly flushed before closing (sync write + flush + small sleep or write sentinel), (2) infra: bump idle/keepalive or disable connection pooling across auth refresh if possible.

jia: customer wants a hotfix today if possible. what minimal change gives best odds?

sophia: infra mitigation fast: increase CloudFront origin keepalive timeout and ensure our origin LB doesn't flush buffers on 401 flows. we'll open a quick deploy to raise idle to 70s for the affected distribution. that should reduce mid-rotate cuts.

marco: app-layer quick fix: add an explicit end-of-stream sentinel event we already support for some models. if streaming path emits `data: {"done":true}\n\n` as final line before closing, it helps clients that parse SSE. but the problem is if the connection dies before that write makes it out. so we should also: on token-swap paths, perform the final write + flush and wait for write confirmation from the OS stack (best-effort).

connor: would you also recommend clients tolerate a trailing partial JSON and attempt to heal by concatenating next chunk after reconnect? mobile clients are flaky doing that.

marco: we don't officially support client-side resume for SSE today (no resume-offset header), so recommend clients avoid reusing the same connection during a refresh. short-term guidance: on 401, cancel and fully open a new fetch; do not attempt to reuse the previous reader. we should add this to our SDK docs.

jia: I'm going to send the customer a brief repro + short-term workarounds: 1) avoid in-place token refresh (reconnect instead), 2) enable retry & request a full response if missing final JSON, 3) ask them to upgrade to our latest node/android SDK patch once released.

marco: I'll scope a small runtime change to add a final sentinel write on token-swap paths + a health log so we can detect if the final write fails. estimate 4-8h work and safe to hotfix behind a flag.

sophia: I'm rolling the infra keepalive bump now (edges/CloudFront) and will monitor. tagging it in the incident: INC-2026-4321.

ci-bot: deploy queued: infra/keepalive-raise -> staging -> canary (sha: d3adb33f) :rocket:

jia: thanks — I'll update the customer and keep this thread posted. next check-in in 30m. :thumbsup:
